question: Which body regulates the professional conduct and practice of nurses in Nigeria?

options.A: National Association of Nigerian Nurses and Midwives
options.D: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: Spot on! The NMCN is the main statutory body that oversees nursing education and practice standards in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T12#GNS321_U2_T12_h1)

question: Why is it important for nurses to understand healthcare laws?

options.A: To avoid personal liability and protect patient rights in clinical settings
options.B: To replace hospital lawyers during lawsuits
options.C: To prescribe medications independently when doctors are absent
options.D: To bypass getting consent from family members in emergencies

explanation: You got it! Knowing your legal boundaries helps you deliver safe care while keeping your license and patients protected. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T12#GNS321_U2_T12_h1)

question: What is the term for a nurse's legal obligation to answer for their professional actions?
explanation: Exactly! Accountability means owning up to both the good and bad outcomes of the care you provide. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T12#GNS321_U2_T12_h2)

question: A doctor writes a medication dose that looks obviously incorrect for your patient. What should you do?

options.A: Ask a junior colleague to give the drug so blame is shared
options.B: Administer the medication quickly so care isn't delayed
options.C: Ignore the order completely and document nothing
options.D: Clarify the order with the prescriber before giving the medication

explanation: Brilliant! Patient safety comes first. Always pause to clarify any unsafe or confusing orders before you administer anything. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T12#GNS321_U2_T12_h2)

question: Which legal concept allows nurses and doctors to treat an unconscious emergency patient without explicit consent?
explanation: Correct! Emergency privilege assumes a patient would want life-saving care when they are unable to speak for themselves. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T12#GNS321_U2_T12_h3)

question: Which of these is required for a patient's informed consent to be legally valid?

options.A: A complete guarantee of a successful medical outcome
options.B: Direct verbal instruction from the lead hospital consultant
options.C: Written approval witnessed by a hospital lawyer
options.D: Voluntary agreement without force or pressure

explanation: Spot on! True consent must be given freely by the patient without any form of manipulation or coercion. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T12#GNS321_U2_T12_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of an advanced healthcare directive?

options.A: To permit nurses to alter medical prescriptions independently
options.B: To guarantee financial compensation for hospital admission
options.C: To guide medical treatment choices before a patient loses the ability to decide
options.D: To protect the hospital from paying taxes on equipment

explanation: You nailed it! Advanced directives let people state their medical wishes ahead of time just in case they can't speak later. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T12#GNS321_U2_T12_h4)

question: Why can carrying out a do-not-resuscitate (DNR) order sometimes be challenging in the ward?

options.A: Nurses have final authority to override any DNR request
options.B: Balancing legal directives, family views, and the duty to save lives is complex
options.C: Advanced directives are automatically the same in every culture globally
options.D: Doctors are legally forbidden from writing DNR orders

explanation: Exactly. Emotions, family expectations, and ethics often clash when dealing with end-of-life decisions, making communication very vital. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T12#GNS321_U2_T12_h4)

question: What is the legal implication if you forget to chart a nursing care entry?

options.A: The hospital automatically wins any civil lawsuit
options.B: The doctor takes full responsibility for the missing note
options.C: The care is legally presumed not to have been performed
options.D: The nurse receives a bonus for saving paper

explanation: That's right! In a court of law, if it isn't documented, it legally didn't happen. Always chart promptly! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T12#GNS321_U2_T12_h5)

question: You realize you forgot to document a vital medication given two hours ago. What should you do?

options.A: Leave it out entirely because late charting is illegal
options.B: Write a late entry clearly labeled with the current time and the actual time of the event
options.C: Wait until the end of the month and add it to the file
options.D: Squeeze the note between previous lines and backdate your signature

explanation: Spot on! Always write a clear 'late entry' with the correct times. Never backdate or try to squeeze notes between lines. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T12#GNS321_U2_T12_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four required elements to prove malpractice?

options.A: Actual physical or financial damages suffered
options.B: Breach of the established standard of care
options.C: Guaranteed financial recovery for the patient's family
options.D: Direct connection between the breach and the injury

explanation: Correct! Financial payout is a possible result of a successful lawsuit, not a baseline legal requirement to prove malpractice occurred. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T12#GNS321_U2_T12_h6)

question: What is the main difference between nursing malpractice and ordinary negligence?

options.A: Malpractice only happens when a patient dies in the ICU
options.B: Ordinary negligence can only be committed by doctors
options.C: Malpractice involves specialized professional skills and breaches of professional standards
options.D: Ordinary negligence carries heavier criminal prison sentences in Nigeria

explanation: You got it! Malpractice specifically applies when a licensed professional's specialized care falls below their training standards. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T12#GNS321_U2_T12_h6)

question: What is the primary role of a nurse acting as a patient advocate?

options.A: Refusing to talk with doctors about care plans
options.B: Suing the hospital administration whenever there is a treatment delay
options.C: Protecting the patient's rights, safety, and dignity when they cannot speak for themselves
options.D: Making all final medical decisions on behalf of the family

explanation: Brilliant! Being an advocate means standing up for your patients and keeping their best interests at heart. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T12#GNS321_U2_T12_h7)

question: You notice a family member pressuring a heavily sedated patient to sign a document. What is your best first step as an advocate?

options.A: Discharge the patient immediately from the ward
options.B: Ignore it because family financial matters are none of your business
options.C: Intervene to stop the activity and notify the nurse-in-charge or security
options.D: Help the family member hold the pen to finish quickly

explanation: Spot on! Protecting vulnerable, incapacitated patients from exploitation is a core part of your duty as a nurse. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T12#GNS321_U2_T12_h7)
